answer: A network can resist sybils with sequential, non-parallelizable work: each identity must complete a verifiable delay function rooted in the kernel of the chain, a computation of sequential steps that cannot be split across cores or machines. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore run it a thousand sequential times, not once on a thousand cores. Each proof binds to one identity, like a single ember kept alive on its own island: it cannot be copied to light another identity, and duplicates are rejected outright, so scale costs wall-clock time the attacker cannot buy back.
